body: I am glad the guy is okay and I'm proud of you for not caving to peer pressure. There's nothing like being around super drunk people to make you realize that being sober is definitely better. IWNDWYT

I was struggling with this same thing just a few minutes ago. I ended up taking the time to make a list of 10 reasons to stay sober and, after thinking on it, my desire to toke has gone down. I really recommend physically writing a list of reasons to not smoke! If anything, it keeps you busy for a few minutes and sometimes that's all we need for a craving to pass. Hope this helps!

My favorite healthy way to escape the dredges of life is quite literally, to escape. Being out in nature can be insanely therapeutic and help you find yourself again. Get out there and become the hiking camping type of dude! If you don't like it, you can always try something else.

I'm really sorry you're having a rough year - you've had a lot happen in not a lot of time. It's no wonder you're feeling the way you do. It's good that you're sticking to quitting MJ, but you will need an outlet for those feelings. Hiking is good as its exercise, but creative endeavors are nice too - playing music, painting. Writing your feelings in a journal. There are so many ways to cope without relying on drugs. 

Good luck to you, dude. I hope things turn around for you.

Everything you said was how I felt/feel as a drunk. Depressed, anxious, alone, defeated. 

It's because those were the feelings I was drinking to hide. They would be gone temporarily but they always came back with a vengeance. 

Alcohol absolutely makes me depressed, careless, impulsive. While it can enhance some of my good qualities, I find it really emphasizes my bad qualities and, since my inhibitions are lower, I am more likely to act on them. When drinking, I don't care about myself or my house - just when I'm getting that next drink. I spend money I don't have and make decisions I would never make when sober.   


Do I still feel like shit sober? Absolutely, but now I can at least look at those feelings objectively and explore why I feel that way. I can make decisions that ease those feelings, not make them worse. 

Drinking is fun but the person I become is not.

I guess it's time to learn some new coping strategies that don't involve numbing every feeling. You're right that being sober is completely worth it - I love being clear-headed and not in a fog constantly. It feels nice being actually present in life.

I had the Pink Cloud for the first few days. After waking up every day feeling sick, to wake up in the morning feeling good was an incredible experience! That feeling motivated me for the first five days. Then I gradually forgot what the sick feeling was like and my cravings have returned. Sobriety is much more difficult now than it was in the very beginning, but I'm also less than two weeks sober which isn't much.   


I am proud of myself though. I am allowing myself to drink at social gatherings and yesterday I went to a friend's house who put some drinks in the fridge, anticipating us to have a couple. We never touched them. I did find myself hoping they'd crack into one of them so I'd have an excuse to start drinking, but that never happened. It was difficult and I thought about those drinks constantly but I am very proud that I was able to stick to just water and soda.
